newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-DALLAS BURN MOVE INTO FIRST AS ALVAREZ STARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DALLAS BURN MOVE INTO FIRST AS ALVAREZ STARS.

text.p: Mexican star Damian Alvarez enjoyed a successful debut, scoring one goal and setting up another as the Dallas Burn recorded a 2-0 victory over the Tampa Bay Mutiny to move into first place in the Western Conference in weekend action in Major League Soccer.
The Burn (6-4) moved past the Kansas City Wizards (4-4), who dropped a 1-0 decision to the New York/New Jersey MetroStars.
Alvarez set up Dante Washington's 22nd-minute goal and converted a penalty kick in the 63rd minute after former U.S. international Cle Kooiman pulled down Washington in the penalty area.
Goalkeeper Mark Dodd made six saves to register his first shutout in a rough game that featured 50 fouls and eight yellow cards. Tampa Bay fell to 5-3.

Goalkeeper Marcus Hanhemann, who made only one save in regulation, stopped four of five shots in the shootout to give the Colorado Rapids (4-6) a 2-1 win over the Colombus Crew (6-3) in Denver, Colorado.
Shaun Bartlett, who scored with two minutes remaining in regulation, and Chris Henderson converted their attempts in the shootout, in which the Rapids prevailed, 2-1.
Second-half substitute Pete Marino scored for Columbus in the 76th minute.
The New England Revolution (5-4) split a pair of shootout decisions.
On Friday night, the Revolution defeated the San Jose Clash, 2-1, in San Jose, California.

Joe-Max Moore, Imad Baba and Erik Imler scored on their shootout attempts in the tie-breaker, won by the Revolution, 3-0. Former Italian World Cup goalkeeper Walter Zenga made one save in the shootout. Troy Dayak had given the Clash (4-6) a 1-0 lead, but Baba equalised.
On Sunday, D.C. United (6-3) defeated the Revolution, 4-2, after playing to a scoreless tie in regulation in Foxboro, Massachusetts.
Nigerian defender Ben Iroha, acquired in a trade with San Jose for Honduran defender Ben Iroha, scored the game-winning shootout goal.

The MetroStars (4-6) broke their league-record scoreless streak at 361 minutes in a 1-0 win over the Wizards as Colombian international striker Antony De Avila scored the lone goal in the 18th minute in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
Former U.S. World Cup captain and goalkeeper Tony Meola made eight of his nine saves in the second half, including one on Zimbabwean international Digital Takawira with six seconds left.
The Los Angeles Galaxy (2-7) snapped a four-game losing streak by defeating the Clash in a shootout, 3-1, after playing to a 1-1 draw in regulation in Pasadena, California.

Cobi Jones, Chris Armas and Robin Fraser converted their chances in the tie-breaker. Brazilian Welton scored for Los Angeles, ending a 317-minute scoreless streak. Lawrence Lozzano tallied for San Jose.
